what_this_is: The Workshop row for the make-a-contact-sheet-of-pictures-or-video-frames folder: a script the person's AI runs on the person's own computer to lay pictures, or frames of a video, out as labelled contact sheets.

payload.label: Make a contact sheet of pictures or video frames (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Lay my pictures, or frames of my video at chosen times or at a steady rate, out as one labelled sheet so I can choose or check them by eye
payload.description: Three kinds of sheet, each from one JSON request. pictures: the given pictures in a grid, each cell the same width and shape (16:9, any w:h, or the first picture's), each picture cut to the cell's middle or stretched into it, labelled below or above with its own words or its file name. frames-at-times: one frame of a video at each given time, or every 1/fps second between two times, stamped with its time, a set number to a row, split over several sheets when asked. frames-at-a-rate: ffmpeg's tile filter over a stretch of a video, frames at a steady rate stamped with their time or frame number, columns x rows a sheet, every sheet or only the first. Every size, colour, font and JPEG quality is a field of the request; nothing is kept between runs.

request.description: A JSON file on the person's computer holding the request, put where {request} is in the command. Its fields: kind (pictures | frames-at-times | frames-at-a-rate) and out (the sheet's file; for several sheets a pattern with {k} for frames-at-times or %02d for frames-at-a-rate); for pictures: pictures [{path, label}], columns, cell_width, cell_aspect, fit, pad, background, label {where, text, font_file, size, strip_px, offset, colour}, quality; for frames-at-times: video, times or every {from, to, fps}, width, columns, per_sheet, label {font_file, size, colour, box, x, y}, background, quality; for frames-at-a-rate: video, fps, start, end, width, height, grid [columns, rows], sheets, jpeg_qscale, nostdin, label {stamp: time | frame, font_file, size, colour, box, x, y}. The README lists every default.

output_schema.description: The last line the script prints: {"result": {"sheets": [the files written], "tiles": the pictures or frames laid out}} (frames-at-a-rate gives tiles_per_sheet), or {"error": what to change in the request}.

get_it: brew install ffmpeg   # only for the two video kinds
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request as a JSON file (the person's pictures or video, where the sheet goes, and any size, colour or font they asked for; leave the rest to the defaults) and pass its path as {request}. Then read the last line: name the sheets written, or say what the error asks to change. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: Ported from a film's contact-sheet scripts (picture grids for thumbnail and preview checks, frames of a preview at chosen times or at a steady rate); every value they fixed is a field of the request
